issues.legal_issue: The prosecution’s failure to explain injuries sustained by accused persons in the same occurrence does not automatically require rejection of its case.
material_facts: Several accused sustained injuries in the occurrence, including a fracture and head injuries.
The prosecution witnesses said that members of the prosecution side used nearby bamboo sticks to repel an attack.
The court accepted the account of an independent eyewitness and other reliable witnesses, supported by the victim’s dying declaration.
The defence account did not appear as probable as the prosecution account.
issues.conclusion: The unexplained injuries did not justify rejecting the prosecution case because the reliable evidence established that the accused initiated the attack and the defence account did not compete in probability.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principles stated in Bhaba Nanda v. State of Assam, AIR 1977 SC 2252, and Takhaji Hiraji v. Thakore Kubersing Chamansingh, (2001) 6 SCC 145, the prosecution is not invariably obliged to explain injuries sustained by accused persons. The court must consider whether the injuries were serious and were sustained in the occurrence, and assess the omission in light of the quality of the prosecution evidence and the probability of the defence account. Non-explanation is a relevant circumstance, not by itself a ground to reject otherwise clear, cogent and credible evidence.

rule.if: criminal_case_evidence_review and serious_same_occurrence_accused_injuries and prosecution_evidence_clear_reliable and defence_version_not_equally_probable

predicates.criminal_case_evidence_review: The court was evaluating prosecution evidence in a criminal case.
predicates.serious_same_occurrence_accused_injuries: One or more accused sustained serious injuries during the same occurrence.
predicates.prosecution_evidence_clear_reliable: The prosecution evidence was clear and reliable, including evidence from witnesses whose account was supported by other evidence.
predicates.defence_version_not_equally_probable: The defence account did not have probability equal to the prosecution account.
predicates.prosecution_case_not_rejected_solely_for: The prosecution case is not rejected solely because serious injuries to accused persons were left unexplained.

issues.definition: When a criminal case has serious injuries to accused persons from the same occurrence, clear reliable prosecution evidence and a defence account that is not equally probable mean that the prosecution case is not rejected solely for the unexplained injuries.

issues.legal_issue: Omissions and deficiencies in an investigation do not undermine a prosecution case whose essential account is established by reliable evidence.
material_facts: The investigating officer did not show certain pegs in the site plan and could not recall whether a bundle of bamboo sticks had been shown to him.
The investigating officer did not send blood-stained earth for chemical examination and no pistol cartridges or bullet components were recovered.
The investigating officer’s work was described as perfunctory.
The court accepted the eyewitness evidence and dying declaration as reliable evidence of the incident.
issues.conclusion: The investigation’s lapses did not materially affect the established core of the prosecution case.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that investigative omissions must be assessed in context and do not, by themselves, displace a prosecution case established by cogent and reliable direct evidence. The judgment applied this principle to the omissions concerning the site plan, physical evidence and recovery of items, without relying on a specific provision or earlier case for this point.

predicates.criminal_conviction_review: The court was reviewing a criminal conviction.
predicates.investigation_omissions: The investigation omitted or failed to record or collect potentially relevant physical or documentary evidence.
predicates.reliable_evidence_establishes_core_event: Reliable evidence independently established the essential events underlying the prosecution case.
predicates.investigation_omissions_do_not_materiall: The investigative omissions do not materially undermine the prosecution case.

issues.definition: In a criminal conviction review, investigative omissions do not materially undermine the prosecution case when reliable evidence establishes its essential events.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for a fatal offence cannot stand where the prosecution fails to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accused’s injury caused the eventual death, even if the accused intended a grievous injury with a dangerous weapon.
material_facts: The assailant intentionally struck the victim’s head once with a sharp, dangerous weapon, causing a severe injury that was sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.
The victim survived for 38 days after the injury, underwent surgery 23 days after it, and died after prolonged hospital treatment.
The prosecution did not provide evidence of the victim’s condition after surgery or establish whether an intervening condition contributed to death.
issues.conclusion: The court set aside convictions for murder and culpable homicide and substituted a conviction for voluntarily causing grievous hurt with a dangerous weapon, because the prosecution had not proved beyond reasonable doubt that the injury was the eventual cause of death.
issues.legal_principle: Section 300, clause thirdly, concerns an intended bodily injury that is sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death. However, the prosecution must also establish beyond reasonable doubt that the injury caused the death. Where that causal connection is not proved, an intentional grievous injury inflicted with a dangerous weapon may support conviction under Section 326 IPC, but not conviction for murder or culpable homicide on the evidence described.

predicates.appeal_from_fatal_assault_conviction: The proceeding was an appeal from a conviction arising from an assault followed by the victim’s death.
predicates.intentional_grievous_injury_with_dangero: The accused intentionally inflicted a grievous injury on the victim using a dangerous weapon.
predicates.victim_survived_prolonged_treatment: The victim survived for a substantial period after the injury and received treatment before dying.
predicates.death_causation_not_proved_beyond_reason: The prosecution did not prove beyond reasonable doubt that the injury was the cause of death, including because relevant evidence about the victim’s later condition was absent.
predicates.fatal_offence_conviction_reduced_to_grie: The fatal-offence conviction is reduced to a conviction for grievous injury.

issues.definition: On an appeal from a fatal-assault conviction, an intentional grievous injury with a dangerous weapon, prolonged survival and treatment, and unproved causation of death result in reduction of the fatal-offence conviction to a grievous-injury conviction.

issues.legal_issue: Firing at a person in an attempt to kill that person can sustain an attempt-to-murder conviction even when the shots miss.
material_facts: The accused aimed and fired a pistol at the victim twice, but neither shot hit him.
The court found the attempt on the victim’s life by firing established beyond reasonable doubt.
The appeal challenged the conviction for the attempted killing.
issues.conclusion: The court upheld the conviction for attempting to murder the victim and dismissed the appeal against it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 307 IPC applies to an attempt to murder. The court found that firing at the victim in the circumstances proved an attempt on his life, notwithstanding that the shots missed; it cited no earlier case for this finding.

predicates.appeal_against_attempted_killing_convict: The proceeding was an appeal challenging a conviction for attempting to kill another person.
predicates.accused_fired_at_victim_to_kill: The accused fired a weapon at the victim in an attempt to kill the victim.
predicates.shots_missed: The fired shots did not hit the victim.
predicates.attempted_killing_conviction_upheld: The conviction for attempting to kill the victim is upheld.

issues.definition: On an appeal against an attempted-killing conviction, firing at the victim in an attempt to kill, even when the shots miss, results in the conviction being upheld.
